sections.title: 1.1 Agentic Loop Lifecycle
learning: Loop pattern: send request → inspect stop_reason → execute tool → append result → repeat.
stop_reason='tool_use' → continue loop. stop_reason='end_turn' → terminate.
Tool results appended to conversation history for next iteration reasoning.
Model-driven decisions vs pre-configured trees.
Anti-patterns: parsing natural language for completion, arbitrary iteration caps, checking assistant text as done signal.

quiz.q: Which signal reliably indicates agentic loop completion?
quiz.explain: stop_reason='end_turn' = only reliable termination signal.

quiz.q: Where do tool results belong between iterations?
quiz.explain: Results appended to history so model reasons over new info.

sections.title: 1.2 Coordinator–Subagent Orchestration
learning: Hub-and-spoke: coordinator routes all inter-subagent communication.
Subagents do NOT inherit coordinator context automatically.
Coordinator responsibilities: decomposition, delegation, aggregation, dynamic selection.
Risk: narrow decomposition → incomplete coverage (e.g., 'creative industries' → only visual arts).

quiz.q: Final report covers only visual arts despite topic 'creative industries'. Logs show coordinator split into digital art / graphic design / photography. Root cause?
quiz.explain: Logs reveal subtasks excluded music/writing/film. Subagents executed correctly within assigned scope.

sections.title: 1.3 Subagent Invocation & Context Passing
learning: Task tool spawns subagents. allowedTools must include 'Task'.
Subagent context MUST be explicit in prompt — no automatic inheritance.
AgentDefinition: description, system_prompt, allowed_tools.
Parallel spawn: emit multiple Task calls in single coordinator response.
Pass structured findings (claim + source URL + date) not raw blobs.
fork_session for divergent exploration from shared baseline.

quiz.q: How to spawn parallel subagents?
options: Emit one Task per turn sequentially
Emit multiple Task calls in single coordinator response
quiz.explain: Multiple Task calls within one response → parallel execution.

sections.title: 1.4 Multi-Step Workflows & Handoff
learning: Programmatic enforcement (hooks, gates) = deterministic guarantee.
Prompt-based ordering = probabilistic (non-zero failure rate).
Critical sequences (verify customer → refund) require gates.
Structured handoff: customer ID, root cause, refund amount, recommended action.
Human reviewer lacks transcript access → summary must be self-contained.

quiz.q: 12% of cases skip get_customer before refund. Best fix?
options: Add few-shot examples showing get_customer first
Programmatic prerequisite blocking refund until verified customer ID returned
quiz.explain: Financial consequence → deterministic gate beats probabilistic prompt approaches.

sections.title: 1.5 Hooks: Interception & Normalization
learning: PostToolUse hook: transform tool result BEFORE model processes it.
PreToolUse hook: block policy-violating tool calls (e.g., refund > $500).
Hooks deterministic; prompts probabilistic.
Use hooks for: data normalization (Unix → ISO 8601), compliance enforcement, refund caps.

quiz.q: When pick hooks over prompts?
options: Critical business rules requiring guaranteed compliance
quiz.explain: Hooks = deterministic; required when failure carries financial/legal/safety cost.

sections.title: 1.6 Task Decomposition Strategies
learning: Prompt chaining: fixed sequential pipeline (predictable reviews).
Dynamic decomposition: adaptive subtasks based on discovery.
Large reviews: per-file pass + cross-file integration pass.
Open-ended ('add tests to legacy codebase'): map structure → prioritize → adapt.

quiz.q: Single-pass review of 14 files: inconsistent depth, missed bugs. Best restructure?
quiz.explain: Attention dilution root cause. File-level passes + integration pass = consistent depth.

sections.title: 1.7 Session State, Resume & Fork
learning: --resume <name>: continue named investigation.
fork_session: independent branches from shared baseline.
Resume risk: stale tool results after file changes.
Sometimes fresh start + structured summary beats resume.

quiz.q: Resumed session after code modifications. Best practice?
options: Inform agent about specific file changes for targeted re-analysis
quiz.explain: Targeted re-analysis avoids full re-exploration cost.

sections.title: 2.1 Tool Interface Design
learning: Tool description = primary selection mechanism. Minimal descriptions → unreliable routing.
Include: purpose, input formats, example queries, edge cases, when-to-use vs alternatives.
Eliminate overlap (analyze_content vs analyze_document with near-identical descriptions).
Split generic tools into purpose-specific ones.

quiz.q: Agent confuses get_customer vs lookup_order (minimal descriptions). First fix?
options: Expand descriptions with formats, examples, edge cases, boundaries
Build routing layer with keyword detection
quiz.explain: Description = root cause mechanism. Low-effort, high-leverage first step.

sections.title: 2.2 Structured MCP Error Responses
learning: MCP isError flag signals failure.
Categories: transient, validation, business, permission.
Return errorCategory + isRetryable + human-readable message.
Generic 'Operation failed' = anti-pattern (blocks recovery decisions).
Distinguish access failure vs valid empty results.

quiz.q: Web search subagent times out. Best error propagation?
options: Return structured context: failure type, query, partial results, alternatives
Auto-retry internally; return generic status when exhausted
Mark as success with empty results
Propagate to top-level handler terminating workflow
quiz.explain: Structured context enables coordinator recovery: retry, alternative, partial proceed.

sections.title: 2.3 Tool Distribution & tool_choice
learning: Too many tools (18 vs 4-5) degrades selection reliability.
Scoped access: agents get role-relevant tools only.
tool_choice: 'auto' (model decides), 'any' (must call some tool), forced (specific tool).
Cross-role scoped tools for high-frequency needs (verify_fact for synthesis).

quiz.q: Synthesis agent verifies facts via coordinator round-trips (+40% latency). 85% simple fact-checks. Best fix?
options: Give synthesis full web search tools
Scoped verify_fact tool for synthesis; complex routes via coordinator
quiz.explain: Least-privilege + role-scoped tool covers 85% case; coordination preserved for complex 15%.

sections.title: 2.4 MCP Server Integration
learning: Project scope: .mcp.json (VCS, shared).
User scope: ~/.claude.json (personal, experimental).
Env var expansion: ${GITHUB_TOKEN} → secrets stay out of repo.
All connected MCP server tools discovered + available simultaneously.
MCP resources expose content catalogs → reduces exploratory calls.
Prefer community MCP servers for standard integrations (Jira, GitHub).

quiz.q: Where store team-shared MCP server config with GitHub token?
quiz.explain: Project-scoped + env expansion = shared config without leaking secrets.

sections.title: 2.5 Built-in Tools (Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Grep/Glob)
learning: Grep: content search inside files.
Glob: path/name pattern matching (**/*.test.tsx).
Read+Write: full file ops. Edit: targeted via unique text.
Edit fails on non-unique match → Read+Write fallback.
Incremental exploration: Grep entry points → Read → trace imports.

quiz.q: Edit fails because target text appears 3 times. Reliable fallback?
options: Read full file + Write modified version
Add more context lines to Edit
quiz.explain: Read+Write fallback = reliable when Edit cannot find unique anchor.

sections.title: 3.1 CLAUDE.md Hierarchy
learning: User-level: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (personal, NOT shared via VCS).
Project-level: .claude/CLAUDE.md or root CLAUDE.md (shared via VCS).
Directory-level: subdirectory CLAUDE.md files.
@import syntax: modularize via external files (max depth 5).
.claude/rules/ alternative for topic-split rules.
/memory command verifies which memory files loaded.

quiz.q: New teammate doesn't receive coding standards. Likely cause?
quiz.explain: User-level config never shared via VCS; must move to project-level.

sections.title: 3.2 Custom Slash Commands & Skills
learning: Project commands: .claude/commands/ (shared via VCS).
User commands: ~/.claude/commands/ (personal).
Skills: .claude/skills/ with SKILL.md frontmatter.
Frontmatter: context: fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint.
context: fork → isolated subagent; prevents output pollution.
Skill = on-demand task; CLAUDE.md = always-loaded standards.

quiz.q: Create /review command shared across team. Where?
quiz.explain: Project-scoped .claude/commands/ → VCS-shared, auto-available on clone.

sections.title: 3.3 Path-Specific Rules
learning: .claude/rules/ files with YAML frontmatter paths field.
Glob patterns: paths: ['terraform/**/*'], ['**/*.test.tsx'].
Loads only when editing matching files → saves context/tokens.
Better than directory-level CLAUDE.md when files spread across codebase.

quiz.q: Test files scattered (Button.test.tsx beside Button.tsx etc). Apply same test conventions to all. Best?
options: Consolidate in root CLAUDE.md with headers
quiz.explain: Glob path rules apply by file type regardless of location → deterministic.

sections.title: 3.4 Plan Mode vs Direct Execution
learning: Plan mode: complex tasks, large-scale changes, architectural decisions, multi-file.
Direct execution: simple well-scoped (single-file fix, one validation).
Plan mode = safe exploration before commitment.
Explore subagent isolates verbose discovery output.
Combine: plan investigation → direct execution implementation.

quiz.q: Restructure monolith → microservices across dozens of files. Approach?
options: Plan mode for exploration + design before changes
Direct execution with detailed upfront prompt
Direct execution; switch to plan if complex
quiz.explain: Architectural decisions + large scale = plan mode hallmark.

sections.title: 3.5 Iterative Refinement
learning: Concrete input/output examples > prose descriptions.
Test-driven iteration: write tests first, share failures.
Interview pattern: Claude asks clarifying questions before coding.
Interacting issues → single message. Independent issues → sequential.

quiz.q: Prose description produces inconsistent transformation results. Best fix?
quiz.explain: Examples disambiguate transformation requirements unambiguously.

sections.title: 3.6 CI/CD Integration
learning: -p / --print: non-interactive mode for CI.
--output-format json + --json-schema: machine-parseable findings.
CLAUDE.md provides project context (testing standards, criteria).
Session isolation: independent review instance beats self-review.
Include prior findings on re-runs → avoid duplicate comments.
Batch API: 50% cost savings, up to 24h SLA, no multi-turn tools.

quiz.q: CI job hangs running 'claude "Analyze PR"'. Fix?
quiz.explain: -p / --print = documented non-interactive mode.

quiz.q: Two workflows: blocking pre-merge check + overnight tech-debt report. Manager proposes batch API for both.
options: Batch only for overnight report; sync for pre-merge
Batch for both with timeout fallback
quiz.explain: Batch SLA up to 24h unsuitable for blocking workflows; ideal for overnight.

sections.title: 4.1 Explicit Criteria Over Vague Instructions
learning: Explicit categorical criteria > 'be conservative' or 'high-confidence'.
Define which issues to report (bugs, security) vs skip (style, local).
High false-positive categories destroy developer trust across accurate ones.
Define severity with concrete code examples per level.

quiz.q: Reduce false positives in code review. Best prompt change?
options: Explicit categorical criteria with concrete examples
quiz.explain: Specific criteria beat confidence-based filtering or vague modifiers.

sections.title: 4.2 Few-Shot Prompting
learning: 2-4 targeted examples for ambiguous scenarios.
Show reasoning: why action chosen over alternative.
Demonstrate output format (location, issue, severity, fix).
Distinguish acceptable code patterns from genuine issues.
Handle varied document structures (inline citations vs bibliographies).
Reduces hallucination in extraction with informal measurements.

quiz.q: Extraction produces null for required fields across varied document formats. Best fix?
options: Few-shot examples showing extraction from varied formats
quiz.explain: Few-shot demonstrates correct extraction patterns across formats.

sections.title: 4.3 Structured Output via tool_use + JSON Schema
learning: tool_use + JSON schema = most reliable structured output.
Eliminates syntax errors; semantic errors remain possible.
tool_choice: 'auto' (may return text), 'any' (must call tool), forced (specific tool).
Required vs optional fields: optional/nullable for absent info → prevents fabrication.
Enum with 'other' + detail string for extensible categorization.
Add 'unclear' enum for ambiguous cases.

quiz.q: Multiple extraction schemas, unknown doc type. Guarantee tool call?
quiz.explain: 'any' guarantees tool call while letting model pick best schema.

quiz.q: Source documents sometimes lack a field. Schema design?
options: Optional / nullable so model returns null
quiz.explain: Nullable prevents hallucination to satisfy required fields.

sections.title: 4.4 Validation, Retry, Feedback Loops
learning: Retry-with-error-feedback: append validation errors to retry prompt.
Retries effective for: format mismatches, structural errors.
Retries ineffective when: required info absent from source.
Self-correction: extract calculated_total + stated_total; flag discrepancy.
Track detected_pattern field for false-positive analysis.

quiz.q: Extraction missing field X. Source doesn't contain X. Will retry help?
quiz.explain: Retries fix format/structure issues, not missing source data.

sections.title: 4.5 Batch Processing Strategies
learning: Message Batches API: 50% savings, ≤24h window, no SLA.
Suited for: overnight reports, weekly audits, nightly test gen.
Unsuited for: blocking pre-merge checks.
No multi-turn tool calling within single batch request.
custom_id correlates request/response; resubmit failed only.
SLA math: 30h deadline + 24h batch → submit within 6h window.

quiz.q: Batch of 100 docs: 5 fail (context limit). Recovery?
options: Identify failures by custom_id; resubmit only failed with chunking
Switch to sync API for all
quiz.explain: custom_id enables targeted resubmission with modifications.

sections.title: 4.6 Multi-Instance Review Architectures
learning: Self-review limitation: generator retains reasoning bias.
Independent review instance > self-review or extended thinking.
Multi-pass: per-file local analysis + cross-file integration pass.
Avoids attention dilution and contradictory findings.

quiz.q: Improve review quality of generated code?
options: Independent Claude instance without generator's reasoning context
quiz.explain: Independent instance catches subtle issues self-review misses.

sections.title: 5.1 Conversation Context Preservation
learning: Progressive summarization risk: numbers, dates, percentages get vague.
Lost-in-the-middle: models reliable at start/end, miss middle sections.
Tool results accumulate disproportionately (40 fields when 5 matter).
Extract case facts into persistent block injected each prompt.
Trim verbose tool outputs to relevant fields only.
Place key findings at beginning of aggregated inputs.

quiz.q: Long support conversation drifts on amounts/dates after summarization. Best fix?
options: Persistent 'case facts' block (amounts, dates, IDs) in every prompt
quiz.explain: Structured facts block survives summarization condensation.

sections.title: 5.2 Escalation & Ambiguity
learning: Escalate immediately on explicit human request.
Escalate when policy silent/ambiguous (e.g., competitor price match).
Escalate when no meaningful progress possible.
Sentiment + self-reported confidence = unreliable triggers.
Multiple customer matches → ask additional identifier, don't guess.
Acknowledge frustration → offer resolution → escalate only if customer reiterates.

quiz.q: 55% resolution vs 80% target. Agent escalates simple cases, attempts complex policy exceptions. Best fix?
options: Explicit escalation criteria + few-shot examples in system prompt
quiz.explain: Root cause = unclear decision boundaries. Confidence/sentiment poorly calibrated.

sections.title: 5.3 Error Propagation in Multi-Agent
learning: Structured error context: failure type, attempted query, partial results, alternatives.
Distinguish access failure vs valid empty results.
Subagents handle transient locally; propagate unrecoverable + partial results.
Anti-patterns: silent suppression, generic statuses, terminating whole workflow.
Synthesis output should annotate coverage gaps.

quiz.q: Subagent encounters transient timeout. Pattern?
options: Local recovery (1-2 retries); propagate unrecoverable with partial results
Mark as success with empty results
quiz.explain: Local recovery for transient; structured propagation for unrecoverable.

sections.title: 5.4 Large Codebase Context
learning: Extended sessions degrade → 'typical patterns' over specifics.
Scratchpad files persist key findings across context boundaries.
Subagent delegation isolates verbose exploration.
Crash recovery: structured state exports + manifest.
/compact reduces context during long sessions (lossy).

quiz.q: After 3 hours codebase exploration, model references 'typical patterns' instead of specific classes. Mitigation?
options: Spawn subagents for targeted questions + scratchpad file with key findings
quiz.explain: Scratchpad + subagents counteract context degradation.

sections.title: 5.5 Human Review & Confidence Calibration
learning: Aggregate 97% may mask poor performance per document type.
Stratified random sampling on high-confidence extractions.
Field-level confidence calibrated via labeled validation set.
Route low-confidence + ambiguous sources to human review.

quiz.q: Reduce human review while maintaining quality?
options: Field-level confidence + stratified sampling per document type/field
quiz.explain: Aggregate hides segment-specific failures; stratification reveals them.

sections.title: 5.6 Provenance & Multi-Source Synthesis
learning: Subagents output structured claim-source mappings (URL, doc name, excerpt, date).
Conflicting credible sources: annotate both with attribution; don't pick.
Include publication/collection dates → temporal differences ≠ contradictions.
Distinguish well-established vs contested findings in reports.
Render by content type: financial → tables, news → prose, technical → lists.

quiz.q: Two credible sources give conflicting statistics. Handling?
options: Annotate both values with source + date + methodology
quiz.explain: Preserve attribution; let downstream/reader interpret discrepancy.
